about.title: Chico Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A product that fails in Chico can be almost anything: a space heater in a rental apartment, a ladder bought for a weekend project, a car part that gives out on SR-99 or the Esplanade. Butte County's roughly 90,000 Chico residents buy the same appliances, tools, medications and vehicles as the rest of the state, and the same defects follow them home. California handles these claims differently from an ordinary negligence case. Under strict liability, you usually do not have to prove the manufacturer was careless. You show the product had a design flaw, a manufacturing error, or a missing warning, and that the flaw caused your injury. That shifts a great deal of weight off your shoulders. What matters most in the early days is holding on to the item, its packaging, and any receipt. LawProactive is not a law firm; we are a free service that connects Chico residents with an independent personal injury attorney who takes product cases on contingency. If a product hurt you, ask questions without cost or commitment.

items.title: Strict Liability Changes the Question
items.desc: In California you generally do not need to prove the maker was negligent. The attorney you connect with can focus on showing the defect and how it caused your injury.

items.title: More Than One Party May Answer
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors and the Chico or online retailer that sold the item can each be held liable. An independent attorney can sort out who belongs in the claim.

items.title: Help Protecting the Evidence
items.desc: The product itself is the heart of the case, so it needs to be kept, not thrown out or returned. We connect you quickly so preservation starts early.

items.question: A part on my car failed while I was driving in Chico. Is that a product case or a crash case?
items.answer: It can be both. Chico recorded 209 injury collisions and 258 people injured in 2025, and while most involve driver error, some trace back to a defective tire, brake, airbag or steering component. If a part failed, keep the vehicle from being repaired or scrapped until it can be inspected. An attorney can evaluate whether a manufacturer or distributor shares responsibility alongside any other driver.

items.question: Do I have to prove the company knew the product was unsafe?
items.answer: Usually not. California applies strict liability to most defective product claims, which means you generally need to show the product had a design, manufacturing or warning defect and that the defect caused your injury. Whether the company was careless is often beside the point. That is a meaningful difference from a standard negligence claim.

items.question: I already threw the broken item away. Can I still do anything?
items.answer: Possibly, though it is harder. Photos, the packaging, receipts, the model number, and any similar units you still own can help reconstruct what went wrong. Recall notices and reports from other consumers may also support the claim. An attorney can tell you honestly what is realistic with the evidence that remains.
